   const target = url.format(parsedUrl)

+  // RFC 7230 3.3.3: if a message is received with both a `Transfer-Encoding`

+  // connection (response queue poisoning). Drop the ambiguous header so both

+const MAX_PATTERN_LENGTH = 1000
+const MAX_CACHE_SIZE = 100
+
+// compiled patterns are cached, so that the same pattern is neither checked nor
+// compiled twice - the cache is bounded, as patterns come from (untrusted) data
+const cache = new Map<string, RegExp>()
+
+const RANGE_QUANTIFIER = /^\{(\d+)(?:(,)(\d*))?\}/
+
+/**
+ * Compiles a regular expression for the "pattern" keyword with a $data reference,
+ * i.e. from data rather than from the schema.
+ * Patterns that are too long or that may cause exponential backtracking (ReDoS)
+ * are rejected instead of being passed to the RegExp constructor.
+ */
+export default function dynamicPattern(pattern: string, flags: string): RegExp {
+  const key = flags + "\u0000" + pattern
+  const cached = cache.get(key)
+  if (cached !== undefined) return cached
+  if (pattern.length > MAX_PATTERN_LENGTH) {
+    throw new Error(
+      `pattern from $data reference is too long (${pattern.length} > ${MAX_PATTERN_LENGTH})`
+    )
+  }
+  if (mayBacktrack(pattern)) {
+    throw new Error("pattern from $data reference may cause exponential backtracking")
+  }
+  const regExp = new RegExp(pattern, flags)
+  if (cache.size >= MAX_CACHE_SIZE) cache.clear()
+  cache.set(key, regExp)
+  return regExp
+}
+
+dynamicPattern.code = 'require("ajv/dist/runtime/dynamicPattern").default'
+
+/**
+ * Conservative check for patterns that may require exponential time to match:
+ * a quantifier that can repeat more than once applied to a group that itself
+ * contains a quantifier or an alternation (e.g. "(a|a)*", "(a+)+", "(a|b){20}").
+ */
+function mayBacktrack(pattern: string): boolean {
+  // whether the current group contains a quantifier or an alternation
+  const stack: boolean[] = []
+  let complex = false
+  for (let i = 0; i < pattern.length; i++) {
+    switch (pattern[i]) {
+      case "\\":
+        i++ // skip escaped character
+        break
+      case "[":
+        i = charClassEnd(pattern, i)
+        break
+      case "(":
+        stack.push(complex)
+        complex = false
+        continue
+      case ")": {
+        const inner = complex
+        complex = stack.length > 0 ? (stack.pop() as boolean) : false
+        const groupQuantifier = quantifierAt(pattern, i + 1)
+        if (groupQuantifier !== undefined) {
+          if (groupQuantifier.multi && inner) return true
+          i = groupQuantifier.end
+          complex = true
+        }
+        complex = complex || inner
+        continue
+      }
+      case "|":
+        complex = true
+        continue
+      default:
+        break
+    }
+    // quantifier applied to a single character, escape sequence or character class
+    const q = quantifierAt(pattern, i + 1)
+    if (q !== undefined) {
+      i = q.end
+      complex = true
+    }
+  }
+  return false

+
+// index of the closing "]" of the character class that starts at index i
+function charClassEnd(pattern: string, i: number): number {
+  for (i++; i < pattern.length; i++) {
+    if (pattern[i] === "\\") i++
+    else if (pattern[i] === "]") return i
+  }
+  return pattern.length - 1 // unterminated - RegExp constructor will report it
+}
+
+// quantifier that starts at index i: "end" is the index of its last character,
+// "multi" is true if it can repeat the preceding expression more than once
+function quantifierAt(pattern: string, i: number): {end: number; multi: boolean} | undefined {
+  switch (pattern[i]) {
+    case "*":
+    case "+":

+    case "?":
+      return {end: lazyEnd(pattern, i), multi: false}
+    case "{": {

+    }
+    default:
+      return undefined
+  }

+function lazyEnd(pattern: string, i: number): number {
+  return pattern[i + 1] === "?" ? i + 1 : i
